description: The only way in for anything the agent does not have: it delivers what it can, says what is missing, and offers the capability by id instead of improvising it or installing it
client_copy: Cuando a tu agente le falta con qué hacer algo, te lo dice y te ofrece la capacidad que lo resuelve.
_comment: SYSTEM, AND NOT BECAUSE ALL FIVE ROLES DECLARE IT. That they do is a fact
about today's roster; what makes this one a default is that it is the
product's own machinery. `capabilities/catalog.json` is the closed list the
client buys from, the adapter draws the card and logs the ask in
requests.jsonl, and the gate hook in policy/hooks/ redirects every blocked
install here BY NAME. A client plugin that wants to say «this needs
something you do not have» has to be able to depend on that being present,
and `system: true` is what lets it.
IT REQUIRES NOTHING, AND THE SKILL.md IS WHY. The ask is not a ticket: it is
a `capability:<id>` mention alone on a line, inside the answer the agent is
already giving -- «El portal la convierte en una tarjeta con el texto ya
escrito y un botón». Nothing is blocked, nothing is approved, nothing is
delivered, so there is no kanban, approval or deliverable in this graph.
That also keeps the system rule satisfiable in the honest direction: a
default may only lean on defaults, and this one leans on none.
NO TAB. There is no Capabilities page in app/app/ and there should not be one
for this: the card is drawn inline in the chat where the agent said what it
could not do, and at hire time by lib/hiring.tsx. A `label` here would have
phase 6 inventing a page for a plugin whose whole surface is a mention.
references/catalog.md IS GENERATED from capabilities/catalog.json by
tools/capability-catalog.py --apply, which now writes into this plugin. The
JSON is the source -- the adapter reads it to draw the card -- and the
markdown is what the agent opens; hand-written twice they drift, and the day
they do the agent asks for an id the portal cannot draw.
